correctness.rationale: On the complex degree-at-most-two space let ζ=e^{iπ/3}. Using ζ²=ζ−1 and λ=(2−ζ)/3, the real-conjugate pair of weights on ζ,ζ̄ has moments (1,1,0), with each absolute weight 1/√3. This certifies the upper bound on the full complex ball. Independently, expanding the modulus square of the numerator gives 21+8 cos t−4 cos(2t)=27−8(cos t−1/2)², with exactly the two stated contacts. Equality after fixing the scalar phase makes both evaluations match p_*. Their difference is c(z²−z+1); subtracting the boundary stationarity equations at the contacts gives the coefficients −(1+ζ) and 1+ζ̄ acting by real part on c, with determinant −3√3/2 in real coordinates. This forces c=0, including when lower-degree polynomials are allowed. The frozen SymPy verifier was inspected, not executed; these exact reductions independently check its decisive identities and uniqueness argument.
